title: POC scoping w/ Northstar Health - Security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a pilot of Redwood Private. Discussed SOC 2/ISO expectations, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logging, KMS requirements, data residency, and benchmarks for workload sizing. Aligned on next steps: send SOC 2 report, schedule SAML configuration session, propose pilot SLOs and timeline.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jason Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Linda Park (Northstar Head of IT), Samir Patel (Security Architect), Tara Nguyen (Product), Evan Brooks (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick recap of security requirements for pilot, confirmed need for SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation, SSO via SAML, RBAC scoping, audit log retention and format, and KMS integration. Agreed on next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jason: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to scope the pilot and make sure security's covered up front. who wants to kick off on your side?
[00:12] Linda: thanks Jason, yeah we got a few goals here. primarily we want to validate private deployment in our VPC and prove the security boundaries — SOC 2 is table stakes for us. also SSO, RBAC and audit log coverage are must haves.
[00:26] Priya: great, that's exactly what we've been doing with other health customers. quick q — are you expecting Redwood Private (VPC) or do you want a dedicated hosted plane with private networking?
[00:38] Samir: we prefer Private in our VPC, air-gap-ish isn't necessary but control of network egress and key management are required. we use an HSM via our cloud KMS.
[00:49] Jason: noted. we can integrate with your KMS and support HSM-backed keys for data at rest encryption; we'll attach the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts post-call.
[00:57] Tara: can you spel out what the SOC 2 package includes? we need the Type II report and details about scoping for systems relevant to PHI-ish data.
[01:11] Marco: sure — we have SOC 2 Type II for our control plane and also ISO 27001 attestation for platform ops, i'll share the certificates and a mapping doc to common healthcare controls.
[01:22] Evan: i'm curious about audit logs — we need immutable logs with 1 year retention and export to our SIEM (Splunk). what's the log format and delivery path?
[01:33] Priya: logs are emitted as JSON line events, include user, token, route, model, and request metadata. we can stream to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export with SSE-KMS. there may be small variances, i'll confirm schema after the call.
[01:48] Samir: retention and tamper evidence are important. do you support WORM or append-only storage?
[01:55] Jason: for Private deployments we can configure append-only buckets and tie lifecycle policies; for stricter needs we can enable storage with object lock and integrate with your SIEM for external immutability.
[02:06] Linda: good. on SSO we use Okta and will expect SAML 2.0. we'll need provisioning (SCIM) later, but initial requirement is SSO and role sync.
[02:18] Priya: we support SAML 2.0 and can do SCIM for automated user provisioning. for the pilot we typically map 3–4 roles: admin, devops, engineer, read-only auditor. how granular do you need RBAC?
[02:31] Samir: least privilege by default — engineers can call models but not change key policies or rollout configs; only security and platform admins get those rights.
[02:41] Priya: that's the common model. we can share our RBAC matrix and you can request custom roles if needed.
[02:50] Tara: what about token handling and PII in logs? we can't have full prompt text stored in any third-party logs for PHI-sensitive flows.
[03:01] Jason: in Private, you control retention and redaction policies. we can mask prompt text in logs and provide a policy that strips or hashes PII; additionally, we can enable local-only KV cache and ensure no retention beyond configured windows.
[03:17] Evan: for benchmarks — we want to simulate 200 qps peak for short bursts and steady 20 qps baseline with 1k token average. what's realistic for your Dedicated nodes vs Private?
[03:30] Priya: on our Dedicated family, a 4-GPU pool handles ~150–250 qps depending on model and token length. for Private, it depends on the instance types you bring; we'll provide a sizing calc. for the pilot we usually start with a small pool and run a 24-hour stress with your samples.
[03:46] Samir: can you run latency and cost tradeoff benchmarks? we'll need 95th percentile latency under 200ms for short completions, but we're flexible on cost if it meets SLA.
[03:58] Priya: yes — our benchmark template collects p95, p50, throughput, and token cost estimates; we'll run with your prompt set. note that quantization or smaller model variants may lower cost but impact quality.
[04:11] Linda: compliance reviewers will ask about encryption-in-transit — do you support customer-managed TLS certs?
[04:18] Jason: yes, for Private you can supply certs, and for hosted we have managed TLS but support custom certs via ACM-like integrations for dedicated routes.
[04:28] Tara: what's the audit process if an incident occurs — do we get playbooks or runbooks?
[04:34] Marco: we maintain incident response runbooks and provide audit logs and post-mortem data for customers under NDA. we'll include a summary in the security pack.
[04:44] Samir: one more on data residency — some of our records must stay in the EU. can you pin regions for Private?
[04:52] Priya: absolutely, Private deployments can be provisioned in specific regions and we can restrict egress. we'll also provide guidance on network ACLs and routing.
[05:03] Evan: regarding RBAC enforcement — we need API-level fine grained controls, e.g., route-level allow/deny. do you support per-route policies?
[05:13] Priya: yes, we have policy scoping per-route and per-model. for pilot we'll propose an initial policy set and iterate.
[05:22] Tara: ok, on timeline — we want a 4-week pilot: week 1 onboarding and infra, week 2 benchmark runs, week 3 security validation, week 4 review and decisions. is that realistic?
[05:34] Jason: totally reasonable. main dependencies are SOC docs, SAML config, and sample workload. once those are in we'll provision.
[05:43] Linda: after the pilot we'll need a formal security assessment summary for our risk committee.
[05:49] Marco: we'll provide a controls matrix mapping and an executive summary; that should help the committee.
[05:56] Jason: i'll recap next steps — share SOC2/ISO, benchmark template, and propose SAML session times.
[06:03] Linda: thanks. any objections from anyone else?
[06:07] Samir: no, let's book the SAML deep-dive.

[06:15] -- (discussion continues with details and clarifications, timestamps sample every few minutes to reflect a longer call) --

[12:00] Priya: quick note — regarding KMS keys we can either bring-your-own-key via your cloud provider or Redwood can manage keys within a customer-controlled partition. we'll document key rotation and access audit.
[18:30] Evan: on log schema could you add correlation IDs for tracing requests across components? that's critical for combing traces with our observability.
[25:10] Priya: yes correlation_id is included in our default schema; we can also inject transaction ids on request creation.
[31:50] Tara: are there any red flags for the pilot from compliance? we want to flag them early.
[32:05] Jason: nothing major — main items are providing your IdP metadata, confirming KMS policy mapping, and agreeing on redaction policy for sensitive prompts.
[38:20] Linda: can you confirm whether raw prompts used for training or telemetry are ever seen by Redwood ML teams?
[38:33] Marco: for Private, customer data does not route to our hosted telemetry unless you opt in; we will provide a telemetry opt-in policy. for hosted, we have strict controls and data-use policies documented in the SOC pack.
[45:00] Samir: we'd like to run an initial 24-hour smoke benchmark next week. can you support that?
[45:12] Priya: yes, we'll coordinate schedule and runbooks, need your sample traffic and test accounts.
[51:00] Jason: ok wrapping up — thanks everyone, we'll send artifacts and calendar invites for the SAML deep-dive.
[51:11] Linda: thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
